newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK governor says sure of PLA troop solution.
newsitem.headline: HK governor says sure of PLA troop solution.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten on Saturday highly praised the behaviour of an advance guard of Chinese troops since they arrived to prepare for Beijing's takeover of the British colony.

Patten also said he was sure there would be a "resolution" of a disagreement between London and Beijing about whether the main group of Chinese troops could enter the territory before it formally returns to China on July 1.

"We obviously want to ensure that the Chinese garrison arrives in the most efficient way, so we are continuing to talk about how the arrival of the rest of the garrison can be managed and handled," Patten told reporters during a visit to the Hong Kong Police Training School.

Senior Chinese officials have said that People's Liberation Army troops need to enter the territory earlier than July 1 to ensure security for Chinese President Jiang Zemin who is attending handover celebrations in Hong Kong.
"I'm sure there will be a resolution because both sides want to see it handled in a low key, sensitive and sensible way," Patten said.
An advance party of 196 PLA soldiers is already in Hong Kong setting up facilities for the eventual military unit that will be stationed in Hong Kong.
Media reports have said Beijing wants to send about 2,000 troops to Hong Kong on the afternoon of June 30.
China has given no figure for the number of troops it plans to eventually station in Hong Kong but at the height of British rule there were about 10,000 London troops in the colony.
Some of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people are wary of a PLA presence because of memories of how the troops put down the pro-democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in 1989.
Earlier this week a mini-row broke out over allegations of special customs treatment for PLA troops already in Hong Kong.
However both Chinese and Hong Kong officials played down the row as simply a language mixup between Hong Kong border guards and PLA troops.

"There has been one incident which I think everyone regrets...but it has so far been the case that the PLA troops in Hong Kong have scrupulously followed all the regulations and arrangements which were put in place a few months ago," Patten said.
